title: VPC edge network visibility + cost-correlation map for Private Console
creator: Aisha Reddy
description: Design a compact, actionable console surface for Private/VPC clusters that combines edge-network path visibility with per-cluster and per-route cost correlation. The goal is to help operators quickly triage networking issues (peering, NAT, route flaps) while understanding the cost impact of traffic patterns and fallback routing. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma screens for a Network > Edge Map view, a correlated Cost Timeline panel, compact status cards for cluster lists, and an integrated rollout health indicator that surfaces when rollouts are impacting cross-region egress costs. Focus on progressive disclosure so operators can drill from a single-pane overview into packet-path-level details and recent upgrade events.
acceptance_criteria: Edge Map prototype shows node-to-node paths, with latency/packet-loss heat overlay and a legend for link health
Cost Correlation panel displays daily egress and per-route token count with a selectable time window and anomaly markers
Status cards for each Private cluster include a compact rollout badge that links to the Rollouts page and shows last 3 changes
Design includes a sampling strategy in copy and settings to avoid encouraging full packet capture; sample rate controls exist in the UI copy
Figma file contains desktop and tablet states, and basic responsive rules for narrow consoles
Design walkthrough recorded and uploaded; feedback from infra engineers and SRE incorporated
comments: 2025-08-05 Aisha Reddy: Kickoff — scoped to Private clusters only. Initial hypothesis: operators want to know if a spike in egress cost is correlated with a specific peering/egress path or with model-heavy traffic. Will prototype three levels: Overview Map, Cluster Detail, Route Timeline.

2025-08-08 Martin Chen: Added constraints from infra — we cannot fetch full pcap; will rely on sampled flow telemetry + existing VPC flow logs. Backend will provide aggregated link metrics per 1m bucket. Design should avoid implying per-packet fidelity.

2025-08-10 Aisha Reddy: First Figma draft uploaded (link below). Implemented heat overlay and anomaly markers. Still TBD: treatments for very large clusters with >200 nodes — switched to cluster-aggregate view by default with expand-to-node as an action.

2025-08-12 Designer review (Sofia Alvarez): Recommend reducing visual noise in map by using edge-thickness for throughput and color only for latency. Also suggested inline help copy explaining sampling and retention limits.

2025-08-14 PM feedback (Leah Ortiz): Add an affordance to pin a cluster to the top and to persist a time-range filter across Console sessions. Also ask infra for cost attribution per model version — flagged as dependency (ENG-47890).

2025-08-17 Engineering sync (Martin Chen): Confirmed backend metrics endpoint will provide per-route egress bytes, per-cluster token estimates, and rollout event timestamps. Sampling rate control will be exposed via settings page — design to include entry copy and microcopy for admins.

2025-08-19 Usability test plan uploaded: 6 internal SRE participants, two scenario flows (triage egress spike, validate rollout-induced latency). Collect task completion times and qualitative feedback.

2025-08-20 Aisha Reddy: Updated Figma with tooltip microcopy, keyboard focus states, and an ARIA-compliant legend. Added a compact mobile fallback for on-call iPad usage. Ready for stakeholder review on 2025-08-21.

2025-08-21 Stakeholder review notes (exec summary): Clear value for correlating cost spikes with routing changes. Ask to add an exportable CSV for cost timelines and a link to open related GitHub PR/Runbook. Minor visual change: use brand accent for anomaly markers, not red, to avoid false alarm.

Follow-ups: Create handoff ticket for engineering (ENG-HO-2033) with component specs and data contract; add localization support ticket for Console i18n team. Schedule engineering grooming for 2025-08-25.
